beats.text: Why does generating long text slow large language models down to a crawl?
In raw self-attention, generating each new word forces the GPU to recalculate every previous token from scratch. That's an O of N squared memory explosion.
Enter the Key-Value Cache. Instead of recomputing history, the model stores past keys and values directly in GPU high-speed VRAM.
When the next token enters, it only projects a single Query vector, fetching all prior context from the cache in constant O of 1 time.
The result? Instant inference speed, a ten-fold throughput boost, and massive VRAM efficiency on long prompts.
